conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: OCCURS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.38.3 "The subject of the entry may be followed within that record description only by data description entries that are subordinate to it" -> OK. OdoResolve walks every ancestor level and refuses any later non-REDEFINES sibling, COBOLNET0856: a direct follower (probe/occurs-p1/sr22_follow) and a follower one level up (sr22_nested_follow) are both rejected. The REDEFINES exemption admits nothing illegal: a following REDEFINES sibling can only redefine the ODO table (§13.18.44 placement), which COBOLNET0855 rejects. A trailing level-66 RENAMES is accepted (sr22_renames_after), consistent with §13.18.45 placing 66 entries after the record's last data description entry. No negative golden pins COBOLNET0856.
rows.rule-text: The subject of the entry may be followed within that record description only by data description entries that are subordinate to it.

rows.subject: OCCURS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.38.3 "Data-name-3 shall not be referenced as a receiving item, except as the operand of a variable-table format SET statement" -> OK; SET Format 14 is the dynamic-capacity-table format (--check 14.9.39.2 "Format 14 (dynamic-capacity-table)" OK). The register as receiver is rejected COBOLNET1523 in MOVE, ADD, COMPUTE, ACCEPT, INITIALIZE, UNSTRING INTO, PERFORM VARYING, DIVIDE GIVING and CALL BY REFERENCE -> probe/occurs-p1/sr32_move ... sr32_call_ref. The permitted Format 14 works: SET C TO 4 / SET C UP BY 1 -> 5 (sr32_set_ok). Treating CALL BY REFERENCE as receiving is the landed PB128 posture. No spec-valued test found pinning the receiving refusal. || Code-location detail (moved from the field by registrar 14e): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/ExpressionBinder.cs#ResolveReceiving (the CAPACITY register screen ~751) | src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Roslyn/PlaceRenderer.cs (backstop ~231)
rows.rule-text: Data-name-3 shall not be referenced as a receiving item, except as the operand of a variable-table format SET statement.

rows.subject: OCCURS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 13.18.38.4 "all data description clauses associated with an item whose description includes an OCCURS clause apply to each occurrence of the item described" -> OK §13.18.38.4 1)). Code: every table element is ONE element type (ElementType) repeated — a fixed table is an array of the one-occurrence element initializer (FieldInit's Enumerable.Repeat / per-occurrence ElementInit), a dynamic table is CobolDynTable<ElementType> seeded by the same ElementInit, so PICTURE/USAGE/SIGN/JUSTIFIED/BLANK WHEN ZERO/VALUE live on the element type and apply per occurrence by construction. PROBE (pinned cobol.exe, out13/probe/occurs-p2/gr1.cob, --std 2023): fixed table E PIC -9(3) OCCURS 3 -> '-005 007-005'; J PIC X(4) JUSTIFIED RIGHT OCCURS 3 -> J(2)='   A'; B PIC 9(3) BLANK WHEN ZERO -> B(1)=spaces, B(3)='012'; S PIC S9(3) SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -> '+000+000-004'; C PIC S9(3) COMP-3 -> packed per occurrence, C(2)=-009. Same five clauses on OCCURS DYNAMIC elements: DD1 edited '-005 007-005', DJE(2)='   A', DBE(1) blank, DSE(2)='-004', DVE VALUE 'ABC' per occurrence ('ABCABCZ  '). SYNCHRONIZED per occurrence is pinned by conformance:2023/l1_sync_occurs_and_no_auto_align (a §13.18.55.4 GR8 golden, one clause only, so not a covering test for this rule). Format 2 shares the element-type model (verified in gr7.cob: TE PIC Z9 edits per occurrence). kb/Work PB851 (open analysis) owns this row's missing witness; test-needed: one golden per format asserting each clause per occurrence. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Formats 1 and 2 all editions; Format 4 from 2014 — Annex E of 2023 lists no change to it, so it predates 2023)
rows.rule-text: Except for the OCCURS clause itself, all data description clauses associated with an item whose description includes an OCCURS clause apply to each occurrence of the item described.

rows.subject: OCCURS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py OK §13.18.38.4 4)): 'The value of integer-2 represents the fixed number of occurrences of the subject of the entry.' Code: FieldInit emits a C# array of exactly item.Occurs (= integer-2) element initializers; CobolTable.At bounds occurrences to 1..table.Length. Probes: gr1.cob group T of five OCCURS 3 tables images as 3 occurrences each; gr14b.cob a fixed OCCURS 2 table raises EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT for occurrence 5 (the fixed count is the highest permissible occurrence number). Constant-name bound (§13.10.3 SR2) accepted per the grammar's occursBound. No spec-derived golden asserts the occurrence count of a Format 1 table as such (char_occurs is characterization only) -> test-needed. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: The value of integer-2 represents the fixed number of occurrences of the subject of the entry.

rows.subject: OCCURS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py OK §13.18.38.4 9)): with a Format 2 record under a RECORD VARYING file/sort-merge description the records are variable length, and without RECORD … DEPENDING ON 'the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1 of the OCCURS clause shall be set to the number of occurrences to be written before the execution of any RELEASE, REWRITE, or WRITE statement'. Code: VaryingLengthArg returns null with no DEPENDING phrase, so WRITE/REWRITE take the record image's length — the §13.18.38.4 GR8 current-extent slice computed by OdoExtent from data-name-1. Probes (out13/probe/occurs-p2): gr9.cob FD RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 2 TO 7, 01 FR. 05 FN PIC 9. 05 FC PIC X OCCURS 1 TO 6 DEPENDING ON FN; WRITE with FN=1,3,6, read back through a second FD with DEPENDING ON RL -> 'LEN 02 [1A]', 'LEN 04 [3BBB]', 'LEN 07 [6CCCCCC]' at --std 85, 2002 and 2023; gr9b.cob RELEASE through an SD with the same shape, SORT … GIVING -> lengths 4 and 2; gr9c.cob RELATIVE REWRITE from FN=2 to FN=5 reads back '5ZZZZZ'. The second sentence is a user obligation (a 'shall' on the program), so no diagnostic is owed. No spec-derived golden exercises an ODO-sized record under RECORD VARYING without DEPENDING -> test-needed. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023
rows.rule-text: If format 2 is specified in a record description entry and the associated file description or sort-merge description entry contains the VARYING phrase of the RECORD clause, the records are variable length. If the DEPENDING ON phrase of the RECORD clause is not specified, the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1 of the OCCURS clause shall be set to the number of occurrences to be written before the execution of any RELEASE, REWRITE, or WRITE statement referencing that record description entry.

rows.subject: OCCURS clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py OK §13.18.38.4 15)): 'Data-name-3 defines a numeric data item that contains the current capacity of the associated table. Data-name-3 shall not be referenced as a receiving operand.' (the second sentence restates §13.18.38.3 SR32, cite.py OK, which excepts the variable-table format SET). Half 1: the register is a read-only view over CobolDynTable.Capacity (= _count, the current capacity §8.5.1.9.1). Probes (out13/probe/occurs-p2): gr1.cob DCAP=3 after three receiving refs; gr14b.cob RCAP 2 -> 4 -> 5 through implicit growth; gr15.cob SET RCAP TO 3 / SET RCAP TO X (X=4) / SET RCAP UP BY 2 read back 3/4/2; MOVE RCAP TO X is legal (sending). Half 2: every receiving position tried is refused COBOLNET1523 ('the CAPACITY register … shall not be a receiving operand except in a SET statement Format 14 (ISO §13.18.38.3 SR30–32)'): MOVE, MOVE to two receivers, ADD, SUBTRACT, COMPUTE, INITIALIZE, ACCEPT, STRING INTO, INSPECT REPLACING, PERFORM VARYING, CALL BY REFERENCE; CALL … BY CONTENT RCAP is accepted (not a receiving reference). Both halves verified. Read half is witnessed by conformance:2014/dyn_capacity_read and conformance:2014/dyn_implicit_grow, but no spec-derived test pins the receiving-operand refusal (no .err or unit test names COBOLNET1523), so test-ref left empty = test-needed (one negative golden per receiving verb family). || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 2014, 2023 (Format 4 only)
rows.rule-text: Data-name-3 defines a numeric data item that contains the current capacity of the associated table. Data-name-3 shall not be referenced as a receiving operand.

rows.subject: OPTIONS paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'If any of the clauses are specified, then there shall be a terminating separator period.' cite.py --check 11.9.3 "If any of the clauses are specified, then there shall be a terminating separator period." -> OK  §11.9.3 1). CODE: `optionsParagraph : OPTIONS DOT (optionsClause+ DOT)? ;` - the clause group and its terminating DOT are one optional unit, so a clause without the period cannot parse, and `OPTIONS.` with no clause needs none. MEASURED (pinned cobol.exe): noperiod.cob (`OPTIONS.` + `DEFAULT ROUNDED MODE IS TRUNCATION` with no period, then DATA DIVISION) is rejected at 2014 and 2023 with COBOL0307 "unexpected 'DATA'. A period may be missing at the end of the previous sentence."; ordered.cob (two clauses + period) compiles and runs (prints 1 = TRUNCATION applied); bare.cob (`OPTIONS.`) compiles and runs at 2002/2014/2023. Both directions of the rule verified at every edition the paragraph exists in (at 85 the paragraph itself is refused, COBOLNET0804). The rule does NOT forbid a trailing period when no clause is written; that case (`OPTIONS. .`) belongs to the general format's independent `[.]` bracket and is adjudicated under FMT-11.9.2, not here. test-ref empty: no conformance negative golden drives the missing-period rejection (tests/conformance/negative has no OPTIONS-period case; tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Integration/SpecFixTests.cs:1024 targets the legacy compiler and does not qualify). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (not 85): the OPTIONS paragraph is a 2002 element (its ARITHMETIC clause's Standard Arithmetic was obsolete in 2014 and removed per Annex E.2 item 21); the seven-clause list is the 2023 format - initialize-clause is new in 2023 (Annex E.3 item 33), the other five non-ARITHMETIC clauses 2014
rows.rule-text: If any of the clauses are specified, then there shall be a terminating separator period.

rows.subject: Object property
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 8.4.3.9.3 'Identifier-1 shall be an object reference; neither a universal object reference nor the predefined object reference NULL shall be specified' OK. Universal half: OoTryBindPropertyReference checks rd.IsUniversal and raises COBOLNET0843 (probe p4 `BAL OF U`, U USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE -> 0843 SR2, plus a redundant 1639). NULL half: `DISPLAY BAL OF NULL` (p3) is rejected (COBOLNET0901 reserved word — the diagnostic does not name SR2 but the source is refused). A non-object-reference identifier-1 falls out of the property path (Pic category check) to ordinary qualification and is not accepted as a property. Both halves verified by probe; no spec-derived test pins SR2 -> test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the object property is part of the OO facility introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002; absent from X3.23-1985)]
rows.rule-text: Identifier-1 shall be an object reference; neither a universal object reference nor the predefined object reference NULL shall be specified.

rows.subject: Objects
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 9.3.6 'The same calling convention shall be in effect for the invocation as is in effect for the invoked method' -> OK §9.3.6 2)). COBOL.NET provides exactly one convention: ENTRY-CONVENTION accepts only COBOL (non-COBOL names refused COBOLNET2385, adjudicated in the entry-convention-clause subject), and >>CALL-CONVENTION is recognized-and-ignored with a documented single-convention disposition (docs/CONFORMANCE.md, 'Recognized-and-ignored compiler directives (§7.3)': 'CALL uses the single .NET managed calling convention'). The invocation's and the method's conventions are therefore always the same one, and the condition is satisfied by construction. Probe out/probe/objects-p1/cc.cob: >>CALL-CONVENTION XYZ before INVOKE R "M" compiled and ran M-OK — consistent with the documented disposition (§7.3.9.3 GR2 b) leaves call-convention-name-1's meaning to the implementor). Vacuous today; it becomes a live check the day a second convention is provided. Test-needed (nothing observable to golden beyond the documented disposition). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO is an ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduction; absent from 1985 — probe p1.cob at --std 85 is refused COBOLNET0900)
rows.rule-text: The same calling convention shall be in effect for the invocation as is in effect for the invoked method.

rows.subject: Operations on dynamic-capacity tables
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.6.9.2 "superfluous elements are not moved and no exception exists" -> OK §14.6.9.2 1)): when the receiving table is NOT dynamic-capacity and the sender's current capacity is higher, superfluous elements are not moved, no exception. §14.6.9.1 (checked OK) makes an ODO receiver a table of capacity = DEPENDING value. Code: GR9 MOVE (MoveEmitter.VariableLengthGroupMove) routes a fixed receiving group through VarCarrierWrite -> RuntimeApi.VarGroupToFixedImage -> CobolVarGroup.ToFixedImage, which CobolString.Store-fits each carried component to its span width (truncation = superfluous elements dropped). Probe out/probe/dyncap/p1.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023 and 2014 identical): dyn sender capacity 4 -> OCCURS 2 fixed receiver gives A=[HH][AAA][BBB] (elements 3,4 not moved, no exception); dyn sender capacity 3 -> ODO receiver with N=2, then N raised to 4, gives C=[AAA][BBB][OL3][OL4] (element 3 beyond the DEPENDING count untouched). No spec-derived MOVE golden exercises the superfluous arm (conformance:2014/pb393_move_varlen_table covers only the shorter-sender arm; BoundaryGroupCorrespondenceTests exercise the CALL boundary, not MOVE) -> test-ref empty. The element-wise MOVE-rule defect (finding 2, filed under GR-14.6.9.2-2) also runs through this path but is the other sentence's obligation. || editions as adjudicated: 2014, 2023 (dynamic-capacity tables / variable-length groups arrive with ISO/IEC 1989:2014; 2023 Annex E lists no change to 14.6.9)
rows.rule-text: If the sending table has a higher current capacity than the receiving table, superfluous elements are not moved and no exception exists,

rows.subject: PAGE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR3 (cite.py --check 13.18.39.4 "If LAST CONTROL HEADING is omitted, integer-5 will be equal to integer-6" -> OK, 3) c)). DataBinder.Reports.cs:794-799 applies a) Heading=1, b) FirstDetail=Heading, c) LastControlHeading = LAST DETAIL if specified else FOOTING if specified else PageLimit, d) LastDetail = FOOTING if specified else PageLimit, e) Footing = LAST DETAIL if specified else PageLimit -- each exactly the spec's arm, and gated on Paged (GR3's 'If integer-1 is specified'). Run probes: gr3d.cob `PAGE LIMIT 10 LINES FOOTING 4.` + 6 x `LINE PLUS 1` details -> lines 1-4 then form feed then 2 lines (FIRST DETAIL defaulted to HEADING=1 per b), LAST DETAIL defaulted to FOOTING=4 per d)); gr3e.cob `HEADING 2 LAST DETAIL 3` -> PF relative LINE PLUS 1 printed on line 4 = FOOTING(defaulted to LAST DETAIL 3 per e))+1. c)'s 'specified' arm is unreachable only because LAST CONTROL HEADING has no surface (FMT/SR1 finding) -- the default computation itself is correct. No spec-derived golden asserts the defaults (every conformance PAGE clause writes the phrases or none are observable) -> test-needed. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Report Writer module, Annex A.4.11; the §13.18.39 text is the 2023 edition's and Annex E records no PAGE-clause change, so no edition gate is derivable from the spec)
rows.rule-text: If integer-1 is specified and any of the following phrases is omitted, a default value for the associated integer is supplied as follows: a) If HEADING is omitted, integer-3 will be 1. b) If FIRST DETAIL is omitted, integer-4 will be equal to integer-3. c) If LAST CONTROL HEADING is omitted, integer-5 will be equal to integer-6, if LAST DETAIL is specified, or equal to integer-7, if FOOTING is specified, or otherwise equal to the page limit given by integer-1. d) If LAST DETAIL is omitted, integer-6 will be equal to integer-7, if FOOTING is specified, or otherwise equal to the page limit given by integer-1. e) If FOOTING is omitted, integer‑7 will be equal to integer‑6, if LAST DETAIL is specified, or otherwise equal to the page limit given by integer‑1.
